text: Investigating the required-flag bug in src/click/core.py now. ETA ~8 minutes.

`prompt` raises `click.exceptions.Abort` (a subclass of `RuntimeError`, defined in src/click/exceptions.py:273, re-exported as `click.Abort`). Both Ctrl+C (`KeyboardInterrupt`) and EOF (`EOFError`) are caught by the same handler in the nested `prompt_func` (src/click/termui.py:144-150) and re-raised as a bare `Abort()`; when `hide_input=True` it first echoes a newline to compensate for `getpass` not printing one. `confirm` does the same (termui.py:236-237).

In src/click/_unicodefun.py, `_verify_python_env` does:

```python
try:
    from locale import getpreferredencoding
    fs_enc = codecs.lookup(getpreferredencoding()).name
except Exception:
    fs_enc = "ascii"
```

So if the `locale.getpreferredencoding` lookup raises, `fs_enc` is assigned the string `"ascii"` (line 13).

Fixed. In src/click/core.py, `Option.__init__` unconditionally set `self.default = False` for any flag without an explicit default, even when `required=True` — so `value_is_missing(False)` was False and the `MissingParameter` check in `Parameter.process_value` never fired. Changed the condition to `if is_flag and default_is_missing and not self.required:`. Now `@click.option('--foo', is_flag=True, required=True)` invoked with no args exits 2 with "Error: Missing option '--foo'." Full suite still green: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.
On it — investigating the no-streams echo bug across src/click/_compat.py, _termui_impl.py and utils.py. ETA ~10 minutes.

A `RuntimeError` (raised at the end of the function, line 100: `raise RuntimeError("\n\n".join(extra))`). The `extra` list starts with the message "Click will abort further execution because Python was configured to use ASCII as encoding for the environment..." plus locale-specific mitigation hints appended on POSIX systems.
Fixed and verified (required flag now raises MissingParameter, exit code 2). Full test suite still green.
Still in progress: the no-streams echo bug across _compat.py/_termui_impl.py/utils.py is under investigation; fix ETA ~8 minutes.

It returns the module-level sentinel `_flag_needs_value` (defined in src/click/parser.py:46, `_flag_needs_value = object()`), i.e. `value = _flag_needs_value` at parser.py:469. `Option.consume_value` (core.py:2862) detects it by identity and then either prompts for the value (if `prompt` is set and not resilient parsing) or substitutes `self.flag_value`. If `_flag_needs_value` is false, a `BadOptionUsage` ("Option {name!r} requires an argument.") is raised instead.
On it — investigating the envvar/flag-value bug in src/click/core.py (test_arguments::test_envvar_flag_value). ETA ~12 minutes.

A builtin `TypeError` with the message `Unknown color '...'`. In `style` (src/click/termui.py:580-590) the `KeyError` raised by `_interpret_color` (termui.py:482, `_ansi_colors[color]`) is caught and re-raised: `raise TypeError(f"Unknown color {fg!r}")` at line 584, and the same for `bg` at line 590 (`_interpret_color(bg, 10)`). `TypeError` is the Python builtin, not a click-defined class.
From `click.utils` — src/click/__init__.py line 67: `from .utils import echo as echo` (definition at src/click/utils.py:204).
On it — investigating the decorator class-preservation bug in src/click/decorators.py. ETA ~12 minutes.

`"Invalid value: {message}"` — i.e. the literal `Invalid value: ` followed by the exception's message (exceptions.py:120). The precedence is `param_hint`, then `param.get_error_hint(ctx)`, and only if both are None does it fall back to that plain form.
Fixed and verified.
Still investigating the no-streams echo bug (root cause analysis in _compat.py/_termui_impl.py/utils.py nearly done); fix ETA ~10 minutes.
Still investigating the envvar/flag-value bug in src/click/core.py; fix ETA ~8 minutes.
Still investigating the decorator class-preservation bug in src/click/decorators.py; fix ETA ~8 minutes.

It returns the items joined with `" / "` with each item wrapped in single quotes: `" / ".join(f"'{item}'" for item in param_hint)` (exceptions.py:14-20). E.g. `["--foo", "-f"]` → `'--foo' / '-f'`. If `param_hint` is not a sequence (a plain string), it is returned unchanged.
On it — investigating the symlink resolution bug in src/click/types.py (click.Path resolve_path). ETA ~12 minutes.

It returns the `color` argument itself, unchanged (globals.py:61-62: `if color is not None: return color`). Only when `color is None` does it fall back to `get_current_context(silent=True)` and return `ctx.color`, or `None` if there is no active context.
It returns `None` (globals.py: `if silent: return None` when the context stack is empty; otherwise it raises a `RuntimeError` telling you to use `click.get_current_context()` within a click command).
`__version__ = "8.0.1"` (src/click/__init__.py, line 75).
`_unpack_args` raises a `TypeError` for a negative nargs value (the `if nargs < 0:` check inside its loop over the nargs specification).

#1: done. #4: fix in progress, ETA ~5 min. #8, #11: root-cause investigation nearly complete, fixes ETA ~8 min. #15: root cause found (click.Path(resolve_path=True) does readlink then realpath, so relative symlink targets resolve against the CWD); fix being applied now, ETA ~5 min. #18: investigating, ETA ~8 min.

Fixed and verified. `_make_cached_stream_func` now returns None when sys.stdout/sys.stderr is None; `echo` returns early when no stream is available; `ProgressBar` and `pager` fall back to a StringIO. Full suite still green (488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed).

Fixed and verified. `Path.convert` did `os.readlink` then `os.path.realpath`, so a relative symlink target was resolved against the CWD; replaced with `os.fsdecode(pathlib.Path(rv).resolve())`. Relative symlinks now resolve correctly; suite still green.
